question: Can a shared color transform predict other visible faces, or all three faces from nominal LDraw RGB?
status: declared before computing this study's model fits
sample: The existing fixed ten color representatives from the 14-image three-face study. Four repeat images are not extra colors. All color-to-LDraw associations remain those already recorded in material-research.json.
primary_hypothesis: A shared gain followed by clipping, applied from the darkest measured face to the other faces, may account for saturated channels better than the reverse direction. This is an output-color approximation, not a recovered shader.
inputs: nominal RGB in the exact supplied LDConfig.ldr
candidates: shared clipped gain in encoded RGB
shared clipped gain and offset in encoded RGB
shared clipped gain in linear-light sRGB
shared clipped gain and offset in linear-light sRGB
three channel-wise affine functions in encoded RGB
3x3 matrix plus RGB offset in encoded RGB
fitting: Least squares in the named space; common gain and gain+offset account for clipping during fitting. Channel affine and full matrix use ordinary least squares before output clipping. No regularization or post-hoc color-specific exceptions.
validation: Leave one color out as a whole, fit on the other nine, predict the omitted color. Repeat for ten colors. Each color has equal weight. Evaluate every candidate, not only the smallest reported error.
metrics: Channel MAE and maximum absolute channel error in encoded RGB levels0..255, with each omitted color prediction and coefficients retained. RGB error is not a perceptually uniform color difference.
transfer_check: Fit on the ten 2x2 representatives and evaluate all12 existing 2x4 controls without refitting. For face-to-face prediction, feed the measured input face of each2x4. For LDraw prediction, feed the same nominal RGB. This checks new images/forms of known colors, not new color generalization.
sensitivity: For the primary left-to-top/right gain model, rerun all ten color holdouts over all81 pairs of input/output one-pixel ROI shifts. This is robustness, not81 independent datasets or a confidence interval.
identifiability: Saturated output channels may lose information; compare both transfer directions. A successful view-specific mapping does not recover light direction, arbitrary surface normals, transparent materials or the manufacturer pipeline.
renderer_policy: Preserve the measured runtime palette. Formula-driven renders are explicit research controls until supported on independent colors and orientations.
